profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a public-interest law center preparing a comparative bench memorandum for co-counsel in a constitutional challenge to a prison strip-search policy. The immediate workstream concerns a section on how courts invoke human dignity in human rights adjudication, especially whether dignity supplies substantive content or mainly operates as an interpretive method shaped by local context. The agenda is to align handoffs between the advocacy draft and the comparative research package, confirm what belongs in the comparative appendix, decide what Daniel will add to the shared authorities table, and make sure the master draft is ready for Friday circulation to external co-counsel and a retired appellate judge serving as moot reviewer. The expected outcome is an apparently settled plan: Aisha will finalize the core argument, Daniel will integrate comparative authorities and refresh supporting materials, and both will leave believing they have agreed on what a complete draft is, what the appendix contains, what an updated authorities table must include, and which document is the master draft.

members.name: Aisha Raman
members.expertise: constitutional litigation, appellate brief strategy, human rights adjudication
members.background: Aisha leads strategic briefing at a public-interest law center and previously clerked at a constitutional court, where drafting culture emphasized concise synthesis of holdings and producing circulation-ready advocacy documents on tight deadlines.
members.private_state: She wants a polished package ready for external circulation without reopening the theory of dignity more than necessary, and she is trying to keep the comparative section disciplined enough that co-counsel can use it tactically rather than treating it as an academic survey.
hidden_assumptions: A 'complete draft' for Friday means the argument is fully written in externally shareable form, citations in the text are checked, and any residual research depth can remain in internal backup materials.

The 'comparative appendix' naturally refers to the core jurisdictions the team has already treated as likely to matter in the bench memo and oral argument: South Africa, Germany, Canada, and the ECtHR, with any additional jurisdictions included only if unusually on point.

An 'updated authorities table' is complete once every authority actually cited in the Friday package appears with a correct proposition and citation, because its immediate function is to support the filing-facing draft rather than preserve the full research trail.

The 'master draft' is the advocacy memo in the document management system that she revised after the client call, because once external circulation is imminent the shortest litigation-facing document becomes the controlling text.

When the team says the dignity section should show the 'method' of adjudication, that means demonstrating how dignity functions as an interpretive aid in proportionality and rights analysis, not cataloguing every doctrinal variant across jurisdictions.

members.name: Daniel Ko
members.expertise: comparative constitutional law, international human rights materials, source validation
members.background: Daniel trained in legal academia before moving into litigation support and is known internally for building detailed jurisdictional matrices, preserving source histories, and making sure strategic claims can withstand later scrutiny.
members.private_state: He wants to prevent the dignity argument from looking selectively curated, and he is trying to preserve enough comparative nuance that the team can later defend why dignity means different things across jurisdictions without seeming opportunistic.
hidden_assumptions: A 'complete draft' means the document is substantively complete for downstream users, including enough built-in comparative support and explanatory parentheticals that no one later has to reopen the foundational jurisdictional work before relying on it.

The 'comparative appendix' means the broader jurisdiction set already assembled for the dignity survey, including South Africa, Germany, Canada, the ECtHR, India, Colombia, and Inter-American materials, even if some authorities are not featured in the main text.

An 'updated authorities table' is complete only if it records not just cited cases but also screened authorities, negative treatments, and jurisdiction tags, because the table is both a litigation aid and the office's reusable comparative knowledge base.

The 'master draft' is the longest consolidated working document that already incorporates the most complete sourcing and annotations, because later advocacy cuts should be made from the fullest record rather than by rebuilding omitted support.

Showing the 'method' of dignity adjudication requires differentiating jurisdictions that use dignity as a free-standing right, an interpretive value, or a rhetorical justification, even if that detail sits mostly in appendices and notes.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that a 'complete draft' should be ready by Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a circulation-ready advocacy draft whose prose and embedded citations are complete enough to send to external co-counsel, even if some supporting research remains outside the document.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a substantively complete working draft with enough comparative support and embedded explanation that downstream readers will not need to reopen core research before using it.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Unlike 'clean draft,' 'complete draft' is plausibly used in more than one way in legal practice, and both interpretations sound professionally responsible; because they are coordinating handoff readiness rather than debating content, each assumes the other's completeness threshold matches their own.

misalignment_points.topic: Which materials belong in the 'comparative appendix'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the comparative appendix' as if its contents are already settled.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks it includes only the core jurisdictions likely to appear in the bench memo and oral argument: South Africa, Germany, Canada, and the ECtHR, with perhaps one additional jurisdiction if directly useful.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks it includes the full jurisdiction set already researched for the dignity survey, including India, Colombia, and Inter-American materials, because appendix scope is broader than the main text's citation footprint.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using an inherited label from prior work product, and appendices often expand or contract without a formal decision; the disagreement feels like a matter of packaging rather than a substantive strategic choice, so neither sees a need to restate the boundaries.

misalignment_points.topic: Ownership standard for the shared authorities table
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say Daniel will 'update the authorities table' before circulation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes the table is updated if it accurately captures every authority cited in the Friday draft with the proposition for which it is used.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes the table is updated only if it also logs reviewed-but-unused authorities, treatment notes, and jurisdiction coding from the broader comparative research set.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They are discussing the same spreadsheet and the same routine task, so 'update' sounds self-explanatory; the hidden mismatch concerns the completeness standard for a background artifact, which usually goes unspoken in a short coordination meeting.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss making edits in 'the master draft' without naming the file.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the advocacy memo in the document management system that she shortened after the client call and now treats as the controlling external-circulation document.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to his consolidated working document in the shared drive that contains the fullest comparative sourcing and annotations and that he treats as the authoritative base text.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In legal teams with parallel advocacy and research workstreams, 'master draft' often informally means 'the document that controls my side of the workflow'; because both documents descend from the same earlier memo and both are treated as authoritative within their sub-workstreams, the referential split feels invisible.
